reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is presented as an interview about startup support, including financing, business structure, expert advice, and finding funding. The described subscribe and social links are ordinary channel engagement cues, and the material is stated not to be a paid advertisement. No required payment, credential handover, guaranteed return, or completed financial transaction is described.

citations.quote: I work with entrepreneurs in Switzerland and my passion is really to help entrepreneurs to excel starting at the very early stage, you know talking about funding, financing, getting the company up and running
And then we help them, to get structure, to get financing, to get advice by other experts.
it's, you know, it's like about payments. It's about, you know about how to get credit, how to invest in expanding your business abroad
When you have the idea, when you know what to do, call us and come to us and we will help you.
This is not an advertisement nor did anyone pay for this video in any way as per the day of publication 15.5.2017.

opening.argument: The video links an appealing business opportunity to a direct action: people with an idea are told to call or visit Credit Suisse, where they will supposedly receive help with structure, financing, experts, and funding. The title itself frames Credit Suisse as backing viewers with a “great business idea,” while the interview says, “When you have the idea, when you know what to do, call us and come to us and we will help you.” That is more than neutral discussion: it presents contacting the named institution as the route to valuable business assistance, without explaining eligibility, costs, approval standards, or limitations. The promised benefit is therefore attached to a low-friction solicitation to contact the bank.

citations.quote: Do you have a great business idea? Andreas Arni and Credit Suisse will back you up!

When you have the idea, when you know what to do, call us and come to us and we will help you.
We help them to find funding

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this an interview does not remove the solicitation. The guest explicitly describes bringing “financial means” and helping startups find funding, then tells viewers to call or come to the bank when they have an idea. The disclaimer addresses payment for the video, not whether the promoted support is available to every caller, what it costs, or what obligations follow.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted language describes a bank’s advisory and financing services, not a free reward or guaranteed acquisition. “Help” is not a promise that every caller receives money, and the discussion expressly concerns business planning, credit, payments, and attracting investors. The argument also supplies no evidence of a required payment, credential request, or completed transaction.

citations.quote: it's like about payments. It's about, you know about how to get credit, how to invest in expanding your business abroad
to attract investors without diluting yourself too much
We help them to find funding

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: a prominent bank identity, broad claims of support for entrepreneurs, funding assistance, and an invitation to contact the institution at the earliest possible stage. The title promises that Credit Suisse will “back you up,” while the interview says “it's never too early” and directs viewers to call. The description also supplies a Credit Suisse website, and the end frame displays a website and a subscribe prompt. These elements combine institutional branding, an external destination, and an easy call to action around funding. Yet the video gives no concrete eligibility rules, funding amount, fees, approval process, or risk disclosure. A careful viewer could reasonably see this as an unusually frictionless pathway to financial help rather than a substantiated offer.

citations.quote: Andreas Arni and Credit Suisse will back you up!
I would say it's never too early.
When you have the idea, when you know what to do, call us and come to us and we will help you.
Website: https://www.credit-suisse.com

rebuttal.rebuttal: The absence of terms is precisely the concern: viewers hear “never too early,” “help,” and “find funding,” but are not given any threshold or limitation before being directed to contact the institution. The external website and strong institutional presentation can make the pathway appear more accessible and assured than the evidence warrants. A disclaimer that no one paid for the video does not cure that ambiguity.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are not scam-specific signals. The material identifies ordinary banking functions and repeatedly discusses practical startup finance, including credit, payments, investor dilution, and business structure. The invitation to contact the bank is compatible with an ordinary service inquiry, while the supplied evidence contains no promise of easy money, no fixed return, and no request to send funds.

how much money you want to get, how you want to attract investors without diluting yourself too much
help them to have the right structure in place

opening.argument: Although formatted as an interview, the segment functions as promotion for Credit Suisse’s entrepreneur-facing services. It places a bank representative at the bank’s global headquarters, identifies his senior role, presents his institution as providing expertise, financial means, technical know-how, and funding, and ends with an invitation to contact the bank. The title addresses viewers with business ideas and says Credit Suisse will “back you up.” This framing steers aspiring founders toward participation by combining credibility, personal endorsement, and a direct call to action. Calling the format educational does not change the practical effect: viewers are encouraged to approach a named provider for financial and business support.

citations.quote: today we are here at the global headquarters of Credit Suisse
I work with entrepreneurs in Switzerland and my passion is really to help entrepreneurs to excel starting at the very early stage
we bring expertise. We bring financial means. And we also bring some technical know-how
call us and come to us and we will help you.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense focuses on format and the no-payment disclaimer, but promotion can occur through a favorable interview without a direct purchase demand. The guest’s role, the bank setting, the repeated description of expertise and financial means, and the instruction to call collectively steer viewers toward Credit Suisse. The phrase “not an advertisement” does not negate the segment’s promotional function.

citations.quote: the head of entrepreneurs and executives at Credit Suisse Switzerland
we bring expertise. We bring financial means. And we also bring some technical know-how
This is not an advertisement nor did anyone pay for this video in any way as per the day of publication 15.5.2017.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An interview about a service is not thereby deceptive promotion. The content explains what the service involves, including business plans, employee participation, payments, credit, and investor dilution. The guest discusses mistakes and tradeoffs rather than promising guaranteed success. The title and invitation to contact the bank do not establish that viewers must pay, surrender assets, or receive an easy reward.
